root_cause:
The DUT control FSM is corrupted so no transaction can ever complete.
Three related RTL defects jointly cause the observed failure: (DISC-01) the
synchronous-reset branch sets busy <= 1'b1, so after reset release the start
gate "start && !busy" is permanently closed and no transaction is ever
accepted; (DISC-02) the round counter is incremented by 2 ("round + 2'b10"),
so round never equals 4'd9 and an accepted transaction would never reach the
completion branch; and in the round==4'd9 completion branch done is explicitly
driven to 1'b0, so a done pulse is never emitted even on completion. Net
effect: after reset release the DUT never returns to idle, never honors start,
and never pulses done -- exactly the observed failure.

The RTL's AES-128 datapath is functionally corrupted (intentional benchmark faults, spec §10). Multiple independent RTL defects jointly corrupt the ciphertext of every transaction: (1) 10 SBOX entries differ from FIPS-197; (2) RCON has wrong values (0x03, 0x81) and is declared [1:10] while indexed with round 0..9 (RCON[0] out-of-bounds / off-by-one Rcon); (3) gm2 reduces with 8'h1d instead of 8'h1b; (4) gm3 = gm2(a)^gm2(a) so gm3≡0; (5) mix_columns uses wrong/swapped xtime-2/xtime-3 coefficients (incl. gm3 on b[4c+3]); (6) shift_rows mis-maps 5 byte lanes; (7) next_round_key slices words at k[126:95]/k[94:63]/k[62:31]/k[30:0], swaps the two RotWord bytes, and chains n1=w1^w0, n3=w3^n1; (8) aes_round applies MixColumns only in the final round on the pre-round state, omits it for non-final rounds, and XORs ~k instead of k; (9) the control FSM loads round_key <= ~key on start and the round==9 state update uses the previous round key (K9) instead of the next round key (K10). Net effect: known-answer, corner, and randomized transactions all emit wrong ciphertext (FIPS-197 vector: 0x31de... instead of 0x69c4...).
